source.title: Unmasking Face Embeddings: Reading, Rendering and Naming with Foundation Models
source.authors: Fizza Rubab; Yi-Ying Tong; Arun Ross

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a simple linear map makes representations usable in another model's space, using retrieval, naming, and decoding outcomes rather than the original representation-similarity measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and prior compatibility work, but does not test convergence with scale, cross-modal alignment rising with model capability, or seed convergence. The results recorded here are the study's own evaluations of linear mapping into foundation-model spaces. The paper also reports random and unaligned controls; some control and secondary-metric results are omitted under the row limit.
record.test_reason: The study fits one least-squares linear map from four face-recognition models (CNN and ViT) into five foundation-model spaces. It then measures how much downstream performance (retrieval, decoding, naming) survives on held-out data against the native ceiling and random/unaligned floors. This bears directly on V4 (a simple linear map with little loss), in a new pairing of face-recognition and vision-language models. It does not measure convergence with scale, across seeds, or shared features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that one closed-form linear map, fit from paired embeddings, lets face-recognition embeddings use foundation-model heads for text retrieval (near native), appearance decoding and name matching, while unaligned and random maps sit at chance. Identity transfers only partially and better from ViT backbones. Loss of fine identity in decoding is attributed to the decoder, not the map. They frame the results mainly as a template-privacy threat.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a centered least-squares linear map fit from paired face and foundation embeddings, akin to prior linear compatibility work, but evaluates retrieval, decoding, and naming rather than the original cross-model recognition task.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with source model and foundation target; retrieval and naming also vary by dataset. The paper reports weaker CNN-source transfer than ViT-source transfer and reduced performance when maps are transferred across datasets.
record.problems: The study evaluates four face sources and a limited set of target models and tasks; some measurements are task-specific proxies for successful mapping rather than direct measures of representation geometry. Cross-dataset transfer is tested only for the stated dataset pairs. Table 3 values do not report uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 2 random-transform and unaligned controls; Table 3 random/unaligned controls, LPIPS, FID and identity-retention measures; Table 4 controls, top-5/top-10 and open-set metrics; Table 5 native/control entries; and the vocabulary-size and exposure analyses in Sec. 7. These are not needed to establish the selected aligned-versus-native mapping outcomes; controls are described in the text and tables.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no measurement of whether alignment increases as models grow.
No test of image-caption alignment rising with model quality. Text is used only as the target model's own interface.

Stitching of intermediate layers, relative representations, and unpaired mapping are not tested. Only paired, closed-form linear maps on final embeddings are tested, into 512–1280-d foundation spaces.
No analysis of recurring neurons, circuits or SAE features.
No comparison of similarity measures or their settings. Cross-dataset transfer concerns map generalisation, not metric dependence.
No test of plateaus or of whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

missing.what: Matched-architecture control: an IR-101 CNN trained with the AdaFace objective on WebFace4M reaches 24.7/21.5/12.1% top-1 naming through CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP, vs 63.0/50.9/26.1% for AdaFace-ViT. This isolates backbone architecture as the driver of linear-map loss.
missing.locator: Sec. 7, Closed-set naming, paragraph after Table 4

missing.what: Open-set watchlist metrics. Aligned AUROC is 0.58–0.86 vs native 0.75–0.94, and aligned DIR@1% is 2–26% vs native 21–56%. Calibrated score margins transfer worse than rank. These are declared as left out but bear on how lossless the map is.
Identity retention after decoding. Aligned FR-cosine is 0.04–0.15 vs native 0.10–0.17 (genuine-match level ~0.5). The authors attribute the low values to the decoder rather than the map.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis but does not test convergence. It is evidence only for V4, via downstream task loss rather than geometry. All four sources are 512-d face-recognition models, and all targets are CLIP-family ViTs. The reader's labels were broadly right, but retrieval states were inconsistent (R01, R02, R16 vs R14). I moved all retrieval rows into the supports group, and split the limits_scope label into naming, decoding and transfer groups. Table 5 rows use within-dataset aligned results as baseline, not native.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no measurement of whether distance geometries align more as models grow.
No comparison of alignment as vision and language models improve; text retrieval tasks do not measure convergence of paired image and caption representations.
No same-architecture, different-initialization comparison or measurement of shared features or subspaces.
Tests linear maps into image-text and diffusion-conditioning spaces via downstream task performance. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, circuits, or SAE features are analyzed.
Does not compare alternative representation-similarity measures or systematically vary their settings. Dataset transfer is reported, but not as a test of similarity-measure dependence.
Does not test convergence plateaus or determine whether shared data or objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality.

relationships.condition: Text-to-face retrieval (UTKFace, CelebA), all four sources into CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP, within-dataset
relationships.reason: Aligned mAP is 82–106% of native and often at or above the ceiling, while random/unaligned stay at ~0.2–0.3 (R01–R24).
relationships.display_finding: Aligned mAP reached 82–106% of native performance, often matching or exceeding it, while random and unaligned baselines remained around 0.2–0.3.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Text-to-face retrieval (UTKFace, CelebA), all four sources into CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP, within-dataset
source_check.reason: This condition group mixes near-native results with partial transfer. ArcFace on CelebA reaches 0.457 versus 0.555 through CLIP (R13), 0.467 versus 0.511 through MetaCLIP (R17), and 0.504 versus 0.569 through SigLIP (R21). Split these scope-limiting conditions from the supporting conditions.

relationships.condition: Identity-level information (closed-set naming), especially for CNN sources mapped into ViT targets
relationships.reason: CNN sources keep only 8–17% top-1 against 76–92% native, and ViT sources reach 25–63%, at most ~73% of ceiling (R25–R36). A matched IR-101 vs ViT control (text only) ties the loss to backbone mismatch.
relationships.display_finding: CNN sources achieved 8–17% top-1 accuracy versus 76–92% natively, while ViT sources achieved 25–63%, at most about 73% of ceiling; a matched IR-101 versus ViT comparison implicated backbone mismatch.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Identity-level information (closed-set naming), especially for CNN sources mapped into ViT targets
source_check.reason: Naming remains substantially below native performance, especially for CNN sources; the matched architecture control supports the qualification. Correct the verdict rationale: native top-1 is 88.7% for CLIP, 70.1% for MetaCLIP and 47.0% for SigLIP, not 76–92%.

relationships.condition: Decoding through diffusion conditioning spaces (Kandinsky 2.2, Stable unCLIP)
relationships.reason: Attribute agreement is 0.77–0.83 vs native 0.83–0.87 and DINOv2 similarity 0.54–0.59 vs 0.68 (R45–R60). The mapping carries appearance but with measurable loss.
relationships.display_finding: Mapped embeddings preserved appearance with losses: attribute agreement was 0.77–0.83 versus 0.83–0.87 natively, and DINOv2 similarity was 0.54–0.59 versus 0.68.

relationships.condition: Map fit on one dataset applied to another (CFP→LFW naming, CelebA→UTK retrieval)

relationships.display_finding: ViT naming accuracy stayed nearly unchanged at 25.4→25.3, but retrieval fell from 0.761→0.610 for KPRPE and 0.734→0.365 for ArcFace, approaching the 0.28 floor.
